correctness.rationale: Exact disjoint/same circular arc decomposition yields a finite-threshold area integral. A global trigonometric defect identity and monotonicity supply the exact inverse-sine boundary. Splitting the rare area into a hyperbolic central square and two edge bands gives both log and additive constants with o(h) uniform errors; h=2epsilon-epsilon² converts to the stated probability. Direct Jacobian u=epsilon^t, w=(1-D)/epsilon and Scheffé yield independent uniform conditional log and deficit marks in total variation. Actual checked standalone numerical integration and 1.2-million-sample Monte Carlo agree; neither substitutes for the proof. Domain 0<epsilon<1 exact and epsilon downarrow 0 asymptotic is explicit.

value.rationale: This measures the natural Euclidean chord generated by independent boundary-arclength samples on the fundamental nonsmooth constant-width body. It exhibits a distinctive epsilon-log terminal probability versus epsilon³-log for area samples and sqrt(epsilon) for the circle at fixed diameter. Beyond an unevaluated first-order exponent, the exact finite-threshold integral, explicit nonlogarithmic coefficient, and independent uniform logarithmic endpoint and conditional deficit marks identify and quantify the two-scale corner/arc geometry. These are reusable precise distributional facts for stochastic geometry and illustrate how chord-sampling methods affect terminal laws.
